text:
mike_support: @jenny customer reported intermittent webhook 403s after our maintenance window. They say only some source IPs are being blocked by their firewall and it's breaking delivery for a subset of events.

jenny_netops: saw a spike in 4xx/5xx traces around the window in the us-east-1 egress logs. Any infra jobs that could change outbound IPs?

devops_bot: SNAT pool rebalance started for us-east-1 at 1834567200, completed at 1834567480. Pool compaction removed ~6 idle SNATs and reallocated mappings.

samir_oncall: that rebalance can change the mapped outbound IPs customers observe. Mike, do we have affected-instance -> old/new IP mapping exported?

mike_support: customer sent their firewall logs showing blocked addresses: 54.33.12.7, 3.21.45.9. They expected 34.22.11.5 and 34.22.11.6 (their allowlist). They've attached sample request/response.

eli_sre: I can reproduce from an instance in that VPC by forcing egress to new SNATs. Example: 
```
curl -v -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"ping":1}' https://customer.endpoint/webhook
> Connected to customer.endpoint (54.33.12.7) port 443
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
```
This matches their logs.

jenny_netops: looks like the customer has hardcoded our older SNAT addresses in their firewall. We sent a general maintenance email but didn't include per-VPC egress mapping changes. Missed communication.

mike_support: confirmed. Apology sent and asked for a short-term allowlist patch. They need immediate bypass for priority webhooks.

samir_oncall: short-term options: 1) provide updated allowlist with new IPs, 2) request customer temporarily widen their firewall, 3) allocate pinned SNAT addresses for that VPC (longer-term). Which should we pursue in parallel?

eli_sre: opened infra ticket INF-4821 to request two pinned SNAT IPs for the customer's VPC (pinning reduces rotation risk). ETA 6 hours. I attached tcpdump/traceroute excerpts showing the new source IPs for verification.

mike_support: I've emailed the customer the immediate allowlist (the new IPs) + rollback steps. They answered that they will patch tonight but asked for an interim workaround.

jenny_netops: interim: we can front their webhooks with a small reverse-proxy under our control that uses pinned egress IPs, but that's an operational cost. Alternatively ask them to add a /24 during the window. I'll draft the proxy plan in a separate ticket.

devops_bot: Note: maintenance reason = SNAT pool compaction to reduce idle allocations and costs. Change was non-disruptive for most customers; customers with explicit single-IP allowlists are at risk.

samir_oncall: action items captured: (A) INF-4821 — pin SNATs for the VPC, (B) support to deliver allowlist + detection query, (C) update maintenance template to include per-VPC egress diffs, (D) add runbook test simulating SNAT compaction.

mike_support: creating a short KB for support engineers that includes quick repro steps and `curl` example, plus the email template for allowlist changes.

eli_sre: postmortem note: classification = "egress-address-reassignment". Recommend we: 1) surface customers with single-IP allowlists into a risk list, 2) offer Dedicated egress IPs as part of onboarding, 3) add an automated pre-notify to customers owning VPCs when SNAT compaction will touch their mapping.

mike_support: keeping thread open until INF-4821 returns confirmation. Will update here when pinning is complete. :thumbsup:

eli_sre: last update: INF-4821 assigned a /32 and confirmed routes at 1834568100; customer confirmed temporary allowlist accepted. Closing when infra confirms NAT translation stable.

mike_support: noted. leaving thread open for 1 business day to watch for regression. last update 1834568120
